## Summary

Benzil and 1,3-diphenylacetone condense to tetraphenylcyclopentadienone. This is sample data; the quantities are not experimentally verified.

## Reagents

| Reagent | CAS | MW (g/mol) | Amount | mmol | Equiv |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Benzil | 134-81-6 | 210.23 | 1.051 g | 5 | 1.0 |
| 1,3-Diphenylacetone | 102-04-5 | 210.28 | 1.104 g | 5.25 | 1.05 |
| Potassium hydroxide | 1310-58-3 | 56.11 | 0.056 g | cat. | cat. |
| Ethanol | 64-17-5 | 46.07 | 20 mL | – | – |

## Procedure

1. Place benzil and 1,3-diphenylacetone in a flask.
2. Add most of the ethanol and fit a reflux condenser.
3. Warm with stirring until the solids dissolve.
4. Dissolve potassium hydroxide in a little water and add it to the warm solution.
5. Heat at reflux for 15 minutes.
6. Cool to room temperature and then in ice.

## Workup and Purification

Collect the crystals by suction filtration, wash with the remaining cold ethanol and dry. Expected yield: 1.35 g (3.50 mmol, 70 %).

## Characterization

Deep purple crystals; expected IR absorption near 1700 cm⁻¹ for the cyclopentadienone carbonyl.

## Notes

1. Reserve a little ethanol for washing.
2. The intense colour helps reveal product formation.
3. Avoid prolonged heating after the reaction.

## Hazards and Waste Disposal

Benzil: may irritate skin and eyes; 1,3-Diphenylacetone: may irritate skin and eyes; Potassium hydroxide: corrosive; causes severe burns; Ethanol: highly flammable; eye irritant; Tetraphenylcyclopentadienone: may irritate skin and eyes. Work in a fume hood; wear gloves and eye protection. Collect ethanol-containing filtrates as organic waste.

## References

1. Furniss, B. S.; Hannaford, A. J.; Smith, P. W. G.; Tatchell, A. R. Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th ed.; Longman: Harlow, 1989.
